Project Description:
Lakshadweep Administration has engaged Cochin Port Authority as Project Management Consultants for providing technical support / consultancy services to UTLA in development of Port and Shipping infrastructures and operation in Lakshadweep Islands. The proposed development consists of: 

•	Refurbishment of the existing 530 m long breakwater
•	Extension of breakwater to an additional length of 490 m to ensure safe entry into harbour
•	Construction of 150 m multipurpose jetty to meet  requirements of Navy
•	Construction of 250 m multipurpose jetty to meet  requirements of UTLA
•	Dredging the basin to (-) 8.1 m CD
•	Berth corner lights and other Navigational aids required for night berthing
•	Development of slipway and ancillary facilities to facilitate fishermen and Navy
•	Development of storage facilities on reclaimed land
•	Redevelop passenger facilitation centre with modern amenities
•	Development of road connectivity
•	Providing utilities services including CCTV with night vision

Project Description: Kadmath island is one among the Lakshadweep group of Islands. The affordable mode of connectivity between the islands & the mainland is HSV and barges  owned by UTLA.   But during the monsoon period, HSVs and barges cannot be operated due to sedimentation and shallow depths (~ (-) 1.5 m CD). The connectivity between the islands gets adversely affected.  The existing northern jetty is in dilapidated condition and doesn’t have sufficient length to accommodate the barges. Hence, a new passenger jetty, south of the existing northern jetty is being constructed, for which the IPZ clearance from LCZMA has been obtained in August 2025. It is proposed to utilize the existing Navigational channel and Turning circle by realigning, widening and deepening it. Dredging of Navigational channel of length 1820 m & width  40 m with depth (-) 3.1 m CD. Dredging of Turning Circle: 100 m dia. to (-) 3.1 m CD depth. The dredge spoil material will be used for beach nourishment in the island.
